plugins.name: eon
plugins.description: Eon MCP server — exposes the Eon AI agent tools and skills for multi-cloud backup, recovery, inventory, and onboarding.

skills.name: aws-onboarding
skills.description: Guide users through connecting their AWS source accounts to the Eon platform. Covers viewing existing connections, deploying the Eon CloudFormation stack to provision the IAM role, registering the role ARN with Eon, and triggering resource discovery.

skills.name: backup-policy-creation
skills.description: Guide users through creating a backup policy in Eon: choosing the policy type, defining the resource selector, configuring schedules with vaults and retention, and submitting the create request. Also covers viewing existing policies before creating a new one.

skills.name: cost-explorer-query
skills.description: Answer Eon customer questions about cloud-resource consumption — how many GB/month or USD/credits an account, project, or department spent on EC2, RDS, S3, Azure, or GCP storage, across any time range, with per-month or per-resource breakdowns. Use whenever the user asks how much was consumed, who is spending the most, top-N resources by usage, or month-over-month cost trends.
headings: Critical gotchas (the rest are in references/api-details.md)

skills.name: gcp-onboarding
skills.description: Guide users through onboarding their GCP cloud accounts to the Eon platform. Covers viewing existing connections, preparing the GCP environment, connecting organizations/folders/projects, and triggering resource discovery.

skills.name: ransomware-remediation
skills.description: Investigate ransomware, malware, and data-anomaly findings on Eon-protected resources, and build a remediation playbook to restore affected resources to their last verified-clean recovery point. Covers counting and listing infected resources, reading security-scan evidence and anomaly graphs, resolving a clean snapshot and restore template per resource, and executing a human-confirmed bulk restore including the multi-party-approval handoff. Use whenever the user asks about ransomware/malware/data-anomaly detections, infected resources, or wants to clean up, remediate, or recover from a security incident.
